commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Merge segment reading.

Fixes #1470 by avoiding the second re-scanning.
Clamp each segment to the bytes still in the stream so the merged
read cannot request past EOF.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Check the size.

Fixes https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/568035737, also in #1470.
Decrypt the length recorded in the PFB segment header once it has
been bounded by the file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: read_pfb_tag (merge-segment commit) reports a segment size clamped to the bytes still in the stream, while T1_Get_Private_Dict (size-check commit) allocates and reads that reported size but sets private_len from the length stored in the PFB segment header. Neither edit overflows on its own. With only the clamp, allocation and private_len both follow the clamped size, so t1_decrypt stays inside the buffer. With only the recorded length, the header length equals the size read_pfb_tag returned, and a header longer than the remaining bytes is rejected by the existing cursor check (or by a failing FT_STREAM_READ) before private_len is updated. The two edits together make the cursor check see the short clamped size, so the allocation is that short count, while private_len becomes the larger on-disk length and t1_decrypt reads past the buffer. The lengths are produced in different functions changed in different commits; agreeing them again means relating the value read_pfb_tag returns to the value T1_Get_Private_Dict adds.
